headline: Thomson Reuters is rolling its CoCounsel Legal AI assistant out worldwide, and the law firm Goodwin has expanded its partnership with Microsoft, Law.com's weekly legal technology roundup reports.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 1: both items date from 14 Oct 2026, before the 16 Oct window, the Law.com body is behind a sign-in wall, and the Thomson Reuters details are the company's own press-release claims.
importance_line: Lawyers working across borders may get one AI research tool for more than 100 countries and territories, and law firms are tying their AI work to big technology partners, but the capabilities are Thomson Reuters's own claims and the Goodwin partnership details are not available.
source: Law.com, with a Thomson Reuters press release
summary: Law.com's Legaltech Rundown, a weekly list of legal technology news, names two moves: the global launch of Thomson Reuters' CoCounsel Legal, its AI legal research assistant, and the law firm Goodwin's expanded partnership with Microsoft. Thomson Reuters said in a 14 Oct 2026 press release that a new Multinational Profile brings legal content from more than 100 countries and territories into one CoCounsel Legal workflow and that the upgraded platform will reach customers in more than 90 countries and territories through 2026, claims that are the company's own.
notes: Law.com's rundown is behind a free-account wall; only the headline and two unrelated snippets (Lineal buying Forentec; Control Risks spin-off) were readable. The Thomson Reuters facts come from its paid press release (PR Newswire via Yahoo Finance Canada, 14 Oct 2026). The Goodwin half rests on the Law.com headline and a Law360 headline of 14 Oct ('Goodwin Expands Microsoft Partnership For Its Proprietary AI'); no text on it was readable, so no detail is given.
